Hi Maya — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) attached (Clearline_MAP_v1.xlsx). Please flag edits or missing stakeholders.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: current latency and cost of model inference for clinical triage workflows (slower than expected during peak hours; P95 frequently >500ms).
- Compliance constraints: data residency and auditability; SOC 2 evidence and ability to run in a VPC are hard requirements.
- Business goal: integrate an LLM-powered summarization/triage step into clinician workflow with P95 < 200ms, 99.9% availability, and maintain or improve current label quality.
- Success criteria for pilot: sustained throughput of 400–600 req/min at target latency; qualitative QA score >= 85% on sample prompts; clearly documented rollback plan.

Proposed MAP (high level) — tentative dates and owners
1) Technical deep-dive & environment review — Sept 22 (Marissa) — agenda: sample payload, expected concurrency, security checklist.
2) POC deployment (sandbox VPC with sample dataset) — Oct 4–18 (Marissa + Connor) — deliverables: deployment runbook, perf baseline.
3) Evaluation window & QA — Oct 19–Nov 2 (Clearline + Redwood) — deliverables: latency report, accuracy eval on 1,000 items.
4) Procurement & contract review — Nov 3–18 (Avery + Clearline procurement) — deliverables: SOW, pricing, SLA addendum.
5) Exec decision & sign — target week of Nov 22 (Maya + Tom)

Open items we flagged on the call
- You mentioned integrations with two EHR endpoints; Can you confirm the expected payload sizes and peak per-provider concurrency?
- Legal: is there an existing vendor addendum or a template we should expect?
- Procurement timeline: you said a Q4 decision window — any blackout weeks we should avoid?

Attachments: Clearline_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan snapshot), redwood-qualifiers.pdf (initial security/qualifiers checklist).

Next steps
